sources.excerpt: Shogi, also known as Japanese chess, is an abstract strategy board game for two players.
Monopoly is a multiplayer economics-themed board game.

The history of Monopoly can be traced back to 1903, when American anti-monopolist Lizzie Magie created a game called The Landlord's Game that she hoped would explain the single-tax theory of Henry George as laid out in his book Progress and Poverty.
Catan, previously known as The Settlers of Catan or simply Settlers, is a multiplayer board game designed by Klaus Teuber.
It was first published in 1995 in Germany by Franckh-Kosmos Verlag (Kosmos).
Super Mario Bros. was first released in Japan on September 13, 1985, for the Family Computer (Famicom).
Pong is a 1972 sports video game developed and published by Atari, Inc. for arcades.
The company was founded in Sunnyvale, California, in the center of Silicon Valley, to develop arcade games, starting with Pong in 1972.
Minecraft is a sandbox video game developed and published by the Swedish company Mojang Studios.
Hanafuda are a type of Japanese playing cards.

Uno, stylized in all caps as UNO, is a proprietary American shedding-type card game originally developed in 1971 by Merle Robbins in Reading, Ohio, a suburb of Cincinnati, that housed International Inc., a gaming company acquired by Mattel on January 23, 1992.
Whist is a classic English trick-taking card game that was widely played in the 18th and 19th centuries.
